Inflation is when prices go up over time, so your money buys less than it used to.

Imagine a loaf of bread costs $2 this year. If inflation is 5%, next year that same loaf costs about $2.10. Your $10 that bought five loaves now buys only about four and a half. Nothing about the bread changed; the money just lost some of its buying power.

Why does it happen? Mostly one of two things:

- **Too much demand:** People have more money to spend than there are goods to buy, so sellers raise prices. Think of a popular concert where tickets sell out, so the price climbs.
- **Rising costs:** If it becomes more expensive to make things (wages, materials, energy), companies pass those costs on to customers.

A little inflation is normal and even considered healthy, since it encourages spending and investment. But when it runs too high for too long, it erodes savings, makes planning harder, and hurts people on fixed incomes most.
